originalTitle: US stocks today: Dow falls 500 points after Trump says Iran deal is 'over'
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the main US stock indexes, including the Dow, went down in value after President Trump said the Iran deal is no longer valid. This news made investors worry about the possibility of more conflict, which caused oil prices to rise. As a result, many stocks lost value, but some chip stocks, like those related to Apple, actually went up due to a recent business deal. The overall mood in the market was also affected by concerns about inflation and slower economic growth. This matters because it can impact the value of investments and the overall economy.

originalTitle: US SEC removes legal obstacle to UBS' crisis-resolution plan
simplifiedContent: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has made a decision that helps UBS, a big bank, with its plan for dealing with financial crises. The SEC said it won't take action against UBS if the bank needs to convert debt into equity (a type of ownership) during a crisis. This decision supports a plan by Swiss regulators to make sure banks can handle problems without needing a bailout. It's a key step in making UBS's plan stronger and more reliable, especially after issues came up during the recent rescue of Credit Suisse. This move helps UBS prepare for potential future crises.

originalTitle: Some US Fed officials considered rate hike on Iran war fallout, June meeting minutes reveal
simplifiedContent: Some officials at the US central bank recently discussed whether to raise interest rates because of concerns about inflation and the impact of the Iran war. Most of them thought inflation would go down on its own, but a few wanted to raise rates right away. In the end, they decided to leave interest rates as they are for now. This matters because interest rate decisions can affect the economy and the stock market. The officials also thought that a rate increase might be needed later this year, which could have an impact on investors and the economy.

originalTitle: Levi Strauss shares slip ahead of Q2 earnings report as investors await impact of FIFA World Cup campaign
simplifiedContent: Levi Strauss, a well-known clothing company, is about to release its quarterly earnings report. Before the report comes out, the company's stock price has gone down a bit. Analysts think the company will say it made 24 cents per share in profit and had $1.52 billion in sales. This would be an increase from the same time last year, with profits going up 9% and sales going up 8.6%. Investors are waiting to see how the company's recent advertising campaign, including its involvement with the FIFA World Cup, has affected its business.

originalTitle: Laser Power & Infra raises  ₹222 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: Laser Power & Infra Limited is getting ready to sell its shares to the public, and before that, it has already collected ₹222 crore from big investors. These big investors, called anchor investors, bought shares for ₹214 each. The company plans to sell more shares to the public, starting from July 9, and hopes to collect a total of ₹742 crore. The shares will be available for different types of investors, including regular people, and will be listed on two main stock exchanges, BSE and NSE, by July 16. This is important because it shows that big investors are interested in the company, which might make others more confident in buying its shares.

originalTitle: SBI Funds Management files RHP for IPO; issue opens on July 14
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management, a company related to the State Bank of India, is planning to sell some of its shares to the public through an Initial Public Offering (IPO). This means that regular people can buy shares of the company. The company will sell up to 203.71 million shares, and the State Bank of India will sell some of its own shares in the company, about 128.33 million. The sale will start on July 14, 2026, and people can start buying shares from then. This is important because it allows the company to raise money and gives individual investors a chance to own a part of the company.
